No malicious network requests, data exfiltration, or unexpected execution occurs during the sourcing of this PKGBUILD or the downloading of sources. All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices and pose no inherent danger during the narrow scope of these commands.

<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard build process for the proton-vpn-qt-app package, which is a Qt GUI frontend for the ProtonVPN CLI. The source is fetched from a legitimate and expected upstream GitHub repository (wheat32/proton-vpn-qt-app) using a git+https URL pinned to a specific tag (v1.10.6), ensuring reproducibility and traceability. The use of `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is common for VCS sources in AUR packages and does not indicate malicious intent, as checksums are not applicable to git checkouts in the same way as static tarballs.

The build process uses standard CMake commands to configure and compile the project, followed by installation into the package directory. A post-install symlink is created for compatibility, which is a harmless and common practice. All dependencies are appropriate: Qt6 libraries, the ProtonVPN CLI, and optional tools like curl and libnatpmp for extended functionality. There are no network operations during build or package phases beyond the initial source clone (handled by makepkg), no use of eval, base64, or obfuscated code, and no suspicious file manipulations.

The package does not download or execute any additional code at build time, nor does it exfiltrate data. All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for a Qt-based GUI application. The source repository and build system are transparent and aligned with the package's stated purpose.
</details>

This script serves a purely administrative purpose and aligns with standard AUR maintainer practices.

While the use of `>` (HTML-encoded `>`) suggests the file may have been viewed or edited in a context that encoded special characters, the actual script would use `>` for redirection. Assuming proper decoding, the script is safe and performs a routine packaging task.
